How does Olympia's weather affect a house for sale?

Olympia is wet, cloudy and mild. It averages about 50 inches of precipitation a year with roughly 75% cloud cover, and November through January are the rainiest months. City streets, creeks and rivers can flood between November and February.

Summer heat is rarer but real: the record high is 110 degrees, set on June 28, 2021, and an average of 6.3 days a year reach 90 degrees. Snow averages around 10.8 inches a season, though it has ranged from a trace to 81.5 inches in 1968 to 1969.

Buyers walking an Olympia house tend to look at the same few things:

  • Roof, gutters and downspouts, since the wet season runs for months.
  • Crawlspace and basement moisture, especially in older homes near the inlet or on fill.
  • Moss, rot and drainage around the foundation.
  • Cooling or ventilation, now that summers can reach the 90s and beyond.

Fixing or documenting these items before a showing shortens the inspection phase. A buyer taking the house as-is still reads the seller disclosure, so answer those questions accurately.

Which Olympia city rules matter when you sell?

Olympia allows up to two accessory dwelling units on almost all lots. Each can be up to 1,000 square feet and 24 feet tall, attached or detached. The city also allows middle housing in every residential zone: up to four units on a lot when zoning standards are met, and up to six within a half mile of frequent transit routes or when at least two units stay affordable for 50 years.

That flexibility can raise what a lot is worth to a builder or investor, so mention it if your lot is large. The city also offers six pre-approved ADU plans on its middle housing page.

Rental owners have a few extra steps. The state Department of Revenue's Olympia endorsement page says the city may require rental registration and, for short-term vacation rentals, an additional permit, both filed through the city's online permit portal. A general city business license costs $30 when reported gross income is above $4,000.

  • Permit Center: City Hall, second floor, 601 4th Avenue E, phone 360.753.8314.
  • Counter hours: Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed Fridays.
  • Inspections and permit status are handled through the city's online permit portal.

If an old project never got a final inspection, call the Permit Center before you list and ask what the permit record shows.

How much real estate excise tax does an Olympia seller pay?

The seller owes Washington's real estate excise tax, plus any local portion set for the city. RCW 82.45.080 makes the tax the seller's obligation. The state portion is graduated: 1.1% on the part of the price up to $525,000, 1.28% on the part from $525,000 to $1,525,000, 2.75% up to $3,025,000, and 3% above that.

The Department of Revenue lists new thresholds for sales beginning January 1, 2027: $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. At the Census median of $486,200, the state portion would be 1.1%, or about $5,348, before the local rate. Ask the Thurston County Treasurer for the local rate that applies to your address.

The tax is due on the date of sale, which the Department of Revenue defines as the date the deed is notarized, whether or not the deed is recorded that day. If the tax is not paid within one month of the sale date, interest applies. The affidavit, deed and payment go to the county treasurer where the property sits. More detail is on the Department of Revenue REET page.

How do Thurston County property taxes work at closing?

Thurston County bills property tax in two halves. The first half is due April 30 and the balance is due October 31, and a due date that lands on a weekend moves to the following Monday. In 2026 the second-half date fell on a Saturday, so it moved to Monday, November 2, which has now passed.

Taxes follow the property, not the owner, and the county does not send new statements when a house changes hands. The Treasurer's FAQ says it is your responsibility to decide how taxes are handled in your closing and to know whether the property still has taxes due for the year. Ask your closing agent to prorate the current year and to pay any unpaid half from sale proceeds.

Sellers who are 61 or older, or retired from a disability, may have a tax reduction or a deferral. Those programs run through the Thurston County Assessor, at 360-867-2200 per the Treasurer's FAQ. A deferral is repaid from the estate, so confirm the payoff with the county before closing.

  • Treasurer's office: 3000 Pacific Avenue SE, Suite 130, Olympia, phone 360-786-5550.
  • Special charges such as stormwater can appear on the same bill and are liens too.
  • Real property is not sold for unpaid tax until three full years of delinquency.

What does an Olympia seller have to hand the buyer?

For a sale of improved residential property, the seller must deliver a completed disclosure statement, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. RCW 64.06.020 sets the form and says delivery must happen within five business days of a mutual acceptance unless the parties agree otherwise.

The buyer then has three business days after delivery to rescind. If you do not provide the statement, the buyer may instead waive the right to rescind before or after the contract. Complete every line, write NA where a question does not apply, and explain any yes answer on an attached sheet.

Disclosure covers what you actually know. Past roof leaks, drainage problems and permit history in an older Olympia house all belong on the form if you know of them.

What are the ways to sell a house in Olympia?

Most Olympia owners choose among three routes, and the same deed, excise tax and tax proration steps apply to each.

  • List with a real estate agent and accept the time showings, repairs and buyer financing take.
  • Sell on your own, which means handling the disclosure form, the contract and the closing paperwork yourself.
  • Take an as-is offer from a cash buyer, which can cut repairs and financing delays, though the price usually sits below a fully prepared listing.

Compare written offers, ask what each buyer expects you to pay at closing, and keep the deed and affidavit timing in mind so the sale date and tax payment line up.

More questions about Olympia, WA

How much is the excise tax when I sell a house in Olympia?

It depends on the price and the local rate. The state portion is 1.1% on the first $525,000 of the sale, 1.28% on the next slice up to $1,525,000, and higher above that, with new thresholds starting January 1, 2027. The Thurston County Treasurer can tell you the local rate for your address.

When are Thurston County property taxes due?

The first half is due April 30 and the second half is due October 31, with weekend dates moving to the next Monday. The 2026 second-half deadline was Monday, November 2, so it has passed. The next first-half deadline is April 30, 2027.

Can I build an extra unit on my Olympia lot before selling?

Often yes. Olympia allows up to two ADUs on almost all lots, each up to 1,000 square feet and 24 feet tall, and middle housing of up to four units in residential zones when standards are met. Call the Permit Center at 360.753.8314 to check your lot before you start.

Who pays the real estate excise tax in Washington, buyer or seller?

The seller. RCW 82.45.080 makes it the seller's obligation, though the buyer can become responsible if the seller does not pay, and unpaid tax can become a lien on the property.

Where do I file the excise tax affidavit for an Olympia house?

With the Thurston County Treasurer, together with the deed and payment, because the tax is paid to the treasurer of the county where the property sits. Your closing or escrow officer normally handles this at signing.

What should a seller know about Puyallup, Washington?

Puyallup is a Pierce County city on the Puyallup River, about 10 miles southeast of Tacoma and 35 miles south of Seattle. The Census Bureau estimates 42,682 residents as of July 1, 2025, a 0.7% dip from the April 2020 estimates base.

Ezra Meeker platted the townsite in 1877, and his hop farm drove growth through the 1880s until the town incorporated in 1890. Today the city is best known for the Washington State Fair, the state's largest annual fair. The city covers about 14 square miles of valley floor.

One detail trips up many sellers. Mailing addresses that say Puyallup also cover unincorporated areas such as South Hill, so check whether your parcel is inside city limits. That decides which permit office, zoning code and utility rules apply, while the county bills property tax either way.

What do the Census numbers say about Puyallup homes?

The Census puts Puyallup's median home value above $550,000 and its average commute above half an hour. The table collects the main QuickFacts figures.

How does Mount Rainier's lahar zone affect a Puyallup house?

Downtown Puyallup and nearby neighborhoods lie within a hazard zone for lahars, which are mudflows that a moderate or large Mount Rainier eruption could send down the Puyallup Valley. The city's rules respond to that risk. Under Puyallup Municipal Code 20.20.010(11)(L), accessory dwelling units are prohibited in the lahar exclusion area, with an exception for land within a half mile of the base of the surrounding elevation of the valley floor.

The city's September 2025 tip sheet explains what owners in that area can still do:

  • Build an addition or remodel that has an internal doorway and is not fully fire-wall separated from the main home.
  • Rent that added space to family or, if not family, to no more than one person.
  • Keep a guest house in a detached building, as long as it has no independent cooking facilities and no one lives there full time, with limited exceptions for family and employees.

If your house has a converted garage, a basement apartment or a backyard cottage, confirm with the Planning Division how the city treats it before you list. An unpermitted second unit can complicate a sale. Call 253-864-4165, option 3, or email Planning@PuyallupWA.gov.

What do Puyallup schools, roads and permits look like for a seller?

The Puyallup School District has 35 schools and serves more than 22,534 students, making it the ninth-largest district in the state. Its boundaries extend beyond the city to South Hill, parts of Tacoma and the Edgewood area. Pierce College Puyallup is a community college in the city.

State Routes 167 and 512 meet at Puyallup, giving freeway access toward Lakewood and the Green River Valley. Sounder commuter trains stop at Puyallup station on weekdays, and Pierce Transit buses and a microtransit zone that launched in 2023 serve the city.

The city Permit Center is on the second floor of City Hall at 333 South Meridian, with counter hours of 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., and the main line is 253-864-4165. Anyone with an open building permit should ask the center to confirm its status.

How much real estate excise tax does a Puyallup seller owe?

The seller pays it under RCW 82.45.080, and the state portion is graduated. Through December 31, 2026, the rates are 1.1% up to $525,000, 1.28% from $525,000 to $1,525,000, 2.75% to $3,025,000 and 3% above. A local portion is added on top, which the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer can quote for your address.

For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue moves the thresholds to $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. The Census median home value of $551,800 sits right at that new line. At that price, the state portion works out to about $6,118 under the 2026 brackets and about $6,071 under the 2027 brackets, a difference of roughly $47.

The sale date for tax purposes is the date the deed is notarized, not the recording date. The affidavit, deed and payment go to the county treasurer. After a payment, a refund request must be filed within four years of the sale and goes to the party who paid. See the Department of Revenue REET page.

How do Pierce County property taxes work at closing?

The first half of property tax is due April 30 and the second half by October 31. The county's FAQ says that because October 31 fell on a weekend in 2026, the second half was due Monday, November 2, a date that has now passed. A bill of $50 or less is due in full by April 30.

For residential property with one to four units, interest of 0.75% per month is charged on the full year's tax beginning May 1 if the first half is late, for tax year 2023 and later. You can still pay the first half plus interest through October 31. Ask your closing officer to settle any late amount from sale proceeds.

Pierce County values property at 100% of market value every year and physically inspects each property about once every six years. An owner who disagrees with the value may appeal to the Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 60 days of a value change notice, whichever is later. Only market value can be argued, not the size of the tax bill.

Seniors and people with disabilities may qualify for a property tax deferral. The state pays the tax, and the deferred amount becomes a lien that must be repaid with interest when ownership transfers, under RCW 84.38. If you hold a deferral, request a payoff figure early. The Assessor-Treasurer is at 2401 South 35th Street, Room 142, Tacoma, phone 253-798-6111.

What are the ways to sell a house in Puyallup?

A Puyallup owner can list the house, sell without an agent, or accept an as-is offer from a cash buyer. All three end with the same deed, excise tax affidavit and tax proration at closing.

  • A listing can reach the widest pool of buyers, with the time that showings and financing require.
  • An as-is offer suits a house with deferred repairs, an unpermitted unit or a conversion in the lahar zone.
  • Ask any buyer what they will pay for, who covers the excise tax, and when they want the deed notarized.

More questions about Puyallup, WA

Can I build a backyard cottage in Puyallup's lahar zone?

No. Puyallup Municipal Code 20.20.010(11)(L) prohibits accessory dwelling units in the lahar exclusion area, with an exception near the edge of the valley floor. A guest house with no independent cooking, not lived in full time, may be allowed.

When is the second half of Pierce County property tax due?

October 31, or the next business day if that date falls on a weekend. In 2026 it was Monday, November 2, which has passed. The next first-half date is April 30, 2027.

How much is the excise tax on a $551,800 Puyallup sale?

About $6,118 in state tax under the 2026 brackets, or about $6,071 if the sale takes place on or after January 1, 2027, before the local portion is added. The date the deed is notarized decides which brackets apply.

Does a South Hill address mean my house is in the city of Puyallup?

Not always. Puyallup mailing addresses cover adjacent unincorporated areas such as South Hill. Check your parcel with the city Planning Division or the county to confirm which rules apply.

What happens to a senior property tax deferral when I sell?

The amount the state paid on your behalf becomes a lien that is repaid, with interest, when ownership transfers. Request a payoff figure from the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer before closing.

How can you sell a house fast in Lynnwood, WA?

The three routes in Lynnwood are a standard agent listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, and a cash sale to a buyer who takes the house as it is. A listing usually reaches the most buyers. A cash sale trades some of the price for certainty and a shorter calendar, which matters when you are relocating, settling an estate, or carrying two mortgages.

Lynnwood homes carry a lot of value compared with most of Washington. The Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home in the city at $686,900, so even a modest percentage gap between a retail price and a discounted offer is a large sum.

  • Your mortgage payoff and any lien or home equity line.
  • Agent commission, if you list, and the cost of any repairs a buyer is likely to request.
  • Real estate excise tax, which the seller usually pays.
  • Months of mortgage, tax, insurance and utility payments while the house waits for a buyer.

Compare the net figure from each route. A cash offer that is lower on paper can come out close once you subtract commissions, repair credits and holding costs.

What do Census figures show about housing in Lynnwood?

Lynnwood is growing and diverse, and about half its households rent. The table below uses the Census Bureau's QuickFacts for the city.

Lynnwood cityCensus figure
Estimated residents, July 1, 202542,132

The roughly even split between owners and renters means many Lynnwood houses, condos and townhomes have a rental history. Buyers who plan to rent it will ask about the lease, so keep a copy ready.

Where is Lynnwood, and how did it develop?

Lynnwood sits in southwest Snohomish County, about 16 miles north of Seattle and 13 miles south of Everett, where Interstate 5 meets Interstate 405. The city covers roughly 7.9 square miles on a plateau that rises 300 to 600 feet above Puget Sound, with several hills and valleys. Edmonds lies to the west, Mountlake Terrace to the south, and unincorporated Alderwood Manor and North Lynnwood areas border it on other sides.

Much of the housing stock traces back to the Puget Mill Company, which created the planned farm community of Alderwood Manor in 1917 and sold 5 to 10 acre plots to people who wanted to leave the city. The area took the name Lynnwood from a 1937 plat along Highway 99 at 196th Street Southwest. Voters approved incorporation in April 1959, the city charter was approved on April 23, 1959, and the opening of Alderwood Mall in 1979 turned the eastern side of the city into a retail and office district.

That history explains the pattern on the ground: older parcels near the Highway 99 and Alderwood Manor roots, and a retail and office core on the east side. When you describe your house to a buyer, say which of those settings it belongs to.

How does light rail change selling a house in Lynnwood?

Link light rail has reached Lynnwood City Center station, and the opening on August 30, 2024 gave homes near the station a direct line to Downtown Seattle and the airport. Sound Transit's 1 Line connects Lynnwood with Downtown Seattle and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, and the 2 Line reaches Bellevue and Redmond. Lynnwood City Center station also works as a bus hub.

Community Transit adds local routes and two Swift bus rapid transit lines. The Blue Line runs on State Route 99, and the Orange Line, which opened in 2024, links Edmonds College, Lynnwood City Center station, Alderwood and Mill Creek. The Census Bureau lists average travel time to work at 29.9 minutes for Lynnwood residents.

If your house is within easy reach of the station or a Swift stop, put the distance and the route in your listing or your pitch to a buyer. Houses farther from the station benefit from highway access, since State Routes 99 and 524 and both interstates serve the city.

Which schools and colleges serve Lynnwood?

The Edmonds School District operates the public schools in Lynnwood, along with schools in Edmonds, Mountlake Terrace and Woodway. Lynnwood High School, Meadowdale High School and Scriber Lake High School are the district's high schools in the Lynnwood area. Edmonds College, which opened in 1967, offers two-year programs, and Central Washington University teaches select four-year degrees on a Lynnwood campus shared with Edmonds College.

Confirm your attendance area with the district before citing a school in an ad.

What permits and rules apply to a Lynnwood house?

The City of Lynnwood's Development and Business Services department issues permits through an online portal, and the Permit Center is at 19100 44th Ave W, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. First confirm that your address is inside city limits, because many properties with a Lynnwood mailing address are not. The city offers an address verification map for that check.

The city's guide lists work that needs no permit, such as fences under six feet, painting, playground equipment and decks that do not exceed 200 square feet. A typical remodel, on the other hand, may need a structural permit, plus electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits when those systems change. Ask the Permit Center what is on file for your parcel so you can answer a buyer's questions about past work.

If your lot has room for an accessory dwelling unit, that can raise interest from buyers. The city's guide says attached and detached ADUs are allowed in the Residential Neighborhood zone, with a maximum ADU size of 1,000 square feet, and that each detached unit needs its own utility meters. The guide lists a minimum lot size of 6,000 square feet, a 10 foot street setback and a 5 foot interior setback for the zone. These rules can change, so check the current code with the Planning Division at 425-670-5410.

For utilities, Snohomish County PUD supplies electricity, Puget Sound Energy supplies natural gas, and the Alderwood Water and Wastewater District supplies tap water. Arrange final readings and account transfers with each as your closing date nears.

What do state rules mean for a Lynnwood seller?

Washington asks most sellers of improved residential property to hand the buyer a seller disclosure statement. RCW 64.06.020 sets the delivery window at five business days after both sides accept the contract, unless you agree on another time, and gives the buyer three business days after delivery to rescind.

The real estate excise tax is the other big state item. The Department of Revenue says it is usually the seller's cost and is payable to the county treasurer on the date of sale. A graduated state schedule applies, with a local add-on, and the Department's rates for sales beginning January 1, 2027 are 1.1 percent up to $551,000, 1.28 percent from $551,000 to $1,551,000, 2.75 percent from $1,551,000 to $3,051,000 and 3 percent above that. Earlier sales use the thresholds of $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. At Lynnwood's median value, a sale price lands in the second band, so the 1.28 percent rate applies to the slice above the first threshold.

Ask the title or escrow company to total the state and local amounts for your price before you accept an offer.

How do Snohomish County property taxes affect a Lynnwood sale?

Snohomish County sets two property tax payment dates, April 30 and October 31, and a mailed payment must carry a postmark on or before the date. If the first half is not paid by April 30, the whole year's tax becomes delinquent, and delinquent charges are assessed on the first day of every month. Taxes under $50 for the year are due in full on April 30. Under RCW 84.56.020, interest on residential property with four or fewer units runs at 9 percent a year, and no penalties apply to it.

The county reassesses property every year as of January 1, mails the assessed value notice in June, and uses that value for the next year's taxes. If you disagree with it, you can talk with an appraiser at the Assessor's Office. To appeal, file a completed petition with the Board of Equalization within 60 days of the notice mailing or by July 1, whichever comes later. The clerk of the board is at 425-388-3407. At closing, expect your escrow officer to split the current tax bill between you and the buyer.

What should you ask a cash buyer in Lynnwood?

Get these items in writing before you agree to anything.

  • The exact price and the closing date.
  • Which closing costs each side pays.
  • Any contingency tied to inspection or financing.
  • A title company handling the closing, with a settlement statement showing your payoff and the excise tax.

Have an attorney read the contract before you sign.

More questions about Lynnwood, WA

Can I sell a Lynnwood house as-is?

Yes, Washington allows as-is sales. You still must give the buyer the seller disclosure statement, which asks about known defects, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. Expect an as-is price to reflect the repairs the buyer will take on.

Does a house with a Lynnwood address always fall under Lynnwood permit rules?

No. The city's permit guide warns that many properties with a Lynnwood address are outside city limits. Use the city's address verification map to find out whether the city or the county handles permits for your parcel.

When do Snohomish County property taxes come due?

The first half or the full year is due April 30, and the second half is due October 31. A mailed payment is on time if it is postmarked by the due date. Missing the April date makes the entire year's tax delinquent.

How long do I have to appeal my assessed value in Lynnwood?

You have 60 days from the date the value notice was mailed or until July 1, whichever is later. File a completed petition with the Snohomish County Board of Equalization. The clerk's number is 425-388-3407.

Who pays the excise tax when a Lynnwood house sells?

The seller usually pays it. The Department of Revenue states that the buyer becomes responsible only if the seller does not pay. The tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, so your closing agent normally deducts it from your proceeds.

What is Lake Stevens like for a home seller?

Lake Stevens is about 35 miles northeast of Seattle and 6 miles northeast of Everett, between Marysville and Snohomish. The city lies on a plateau above the Snohomish River delta, with the Cascade foothills to the east. The lake itself is the largest and deepest in Snohomish County, at 1,040 acres, an average depth of 64 feet and 7.1 miles of shoreline.

The area was named for territorial governor Isaac Stevens in 1859. The Rucker Brothers opened a shingle mill in 1907 and filed the town plat in 1908. A fire damaged the mill in 1919, and a second fire in 1925 closed it for good. The shoreline was split into summer-home lots by the mid-1920s. Residents voted 299 to 40 on November 19, 1960 to incorporate, and suburban growth followed.

The city names several neighborhoods and planning areas:

  • Cavalero Hill: a designated neighborhood and planning area.
  • Frontier Village: the shopping district at State Routes 9 and 204.
  • Hartford Industrial Area: home to aerospace manufacturer Cobalt Enterprises.
  • Machias: a community that formed along the railway in 1890.

How do schools and commutes shape buyer interest in Lake Stevens?

The Lake Stevens School District serves the city and part of southeastern Marysville. It has one high school, Lake Stevens High School, which opened on its current campus in 1979 and had a renovation that opened its first phase in November 2019. The district also runs a mid-high school for grades 8 and 9, two middle schools and seven elementary schools.

Commutes run long. The Census mean is 35.2 minutes. A 2018 estimate had 20 percent of working residents commuting to Everett, 13 percent to Seattle and 4 percent to Bellevue, with 6.3 percent working inside the city. Three state highways cross the city: State Route 9, State Route 92 and State Route 204. Four roundabouts replaced the State Route 9 and 204 intersection in 2023. The Hewitt Avenue Trestle carries US 2 to Everett and is frequently congested. Community Transit provides bus service to Everett, Granite Falls, Lynnwood, Marysville and Snohomish, plus a peak-hour express to Lynnwood City Center station.

Retail is concentrated at Frontier Village, and a Costco opened at State Route 9 and 20th Street Southeast in December 2022. Buyers who work in Everett or Seattle will price the drive, so a seller who can show a short route to the highway has something to talk about.

What are the short-term rental rules in Lake Stevens?

Lake Stevens regulates short-term rentals (under 30 days) in Lake Stevens Municipal Code 14.44.064 under Ordinance 1139. The city's FAQ lists these limits:

  • An owner or operator must live on the property as a primary residence at least 240 days a year, unless their permanent residence is in the Lake Stevens Urban Growth Area.
  • Only one rental unit per property, which may be the main house, an accessory dwelling unit or a duplex unit.
  • No more than 50 licenses active citywide, and properties with licenses must be at least 150 feet apart.
  • One off-street parking stall per two bedrooms, each at least nine feet by 19 feet.
  • No use as a paid venue for weddings, banquets or fundraisers.

A city business license and a short-term rental permit are both required. The FAQ lists a $500 application fee and a $100 annual renewal; confirm current amounts with the city at (425) 622-9400. A buyer who wants to keep the rental income should ask the Planning and Community Development Department whether the permit stays with the property or must be reissued to a new owner.

How does Snohomish County handle excise tax and recording?

A deed cannot be recorded in Snohomish County until the Treasurer's Office has reviewed it for real estate excise tax and the tax, if owed, has been paid in full. The review covers many conveyance documents, including statutory warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, transfer on death deeds, personal representative deeds, trustee's deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure. Questions go to the Treasurer's excise staff at 425-388-3366.

The Department of Revenue says the seller usually pays the tax and that it is due on the date of sale whenever the deed is recorded. The Recording Division is in the Drewel Building at 3000 Rockefeller Avenue in Everett. Ask your escrow officer to send the excise affidavit and deed together so recording is not held up.

When are Snohomish County property taxes due, and how can you contest value?

The county's calendar sets taxes as payable from February 15, with the first half due April 30 and the second half October 31. If the first half is not paid by April 30, the full year becomes delinquent and interest or penalty applies on the whole amount under RCW 84.56.020, assessed on the first of each month. The second-half 2026 date has passed, and the next first-half deadline is April 30, 2027.

To dispute an assessed value, a petition must reach the Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within the later window the notice states. RCW 84.40.038 sets the filing rules and allows late filing in narrow cases. January 1 is the valuation date, so a sale at a price that differs sharply from the assessed value is a useful reference when you file.

What must a Lake Stevens seller disclose?

The form under RCW 64.06.020 asks whether the property is inside a fire protection district, whether the roof has leaked in the past five years, and about sewer service. Lake Stevens homes may use the Lake Stevens Sewer District, so check your bill and answer accurately. The buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind unless the parties agreed otherwise in writing.

More questions about Lake Stevens, WA

Can I sell a Lake Stevens house that needs repairs?

Yes. A cash buyer can purchase it as-is, and a listing buyer can negotiate repairs. The seller disclosure form still asks about roof leaks, structural problems and similar items.

Do I need a permit to keep a short-term rental in Lake Stevens?

Yes. Lake Stevens requires both a business license and a short-term rental permit, and only one rental unit per property is allowed. Confirm fees and transfer rules with the city before you sell.

Who pays real estate excise tax on a Lake Stevens sale?

The seller usually pays, according to the Department of Revenue. In Snohomish County the Treasurer's Office must review the deed and receive the tax before the deed is recorded.

When are Snohomish County property taxes due?

The first half is due April 30 and the second half October 31. Taxes can be paid on or after February 15, and a first-half miss makes the full year delinquent.

How far is Lake Stevens from Everett and Seattle?

Lake Stevens is about 6 miles northeast of Everett and 35 miles northeast of Seattle. The Census Bureau puts the mean travel time to work at 35.2 minutes.

What are the ways to sell a house fast in Longview, WA?

A Longview homeowner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house in its current condition. The right choice depends on how soon you need to close, how much work the house needs, and how much of the sale price you are willing to give up for speed.

Before you compare routes, gather these four items.

  • The parcel number and your latest property tax statement from the Cowlitz County Treasurer.
  • A payoff figure from each lender or lienholder on the house.
  • A list of repairs, additions and remodels, with permit numbers where they exist.
  • The completed seller disclosure statement that Washington requires for most home sales.

A traditional listing usually brings the widest pool of buyers and the highest price, but it also brings showings, inspections and a buyer's financing timeline. A cash offer trims all of that, and the trade is a lower number.

What do the Census numbers say about Longview homes?

Longview is a city of about 38,000 people, and its housing costs sit well below the King and Snohomish County suburbs to the north. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page gives the following figures for the city.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts. The median home value is a survey estimate for owner-occupied homes, so treat it as background and get a real valuation for your own house.

Only a little over half of Longview households own their home, so rentals make up a big part of the housing stock. If a tenant lives in your house, review the lease before you promise a closing date.

How did Longview's planned layout shape its houses?

Longview was designed on paper before it was built. The Long-Bell Lumber Company bought timberland in Cowlitz County in 1918, and by 1921 the company had hired St. Louis planner George Kessler to lay out a city for the workers its two mills would need. Kessler modeled the plan on the nation's capital, with elements of Roman city planning, and the city was incorporated on February 14, 1924.

That history explains why the older parts of Longview look different from a town that grew lot by lot. The Civic Center is a National Register historic district, and many buildings from the 1923 to 1934 growth period show Georgian-revival, Tudor and craftsman styles. If your house comes from that era, its age and design can appeal to buyers who want character, and they can also bring older wiring, plumbing and foundations that an inspector will flag. Suburban neighborhoods in the western valley came later, in the 1960s.

The city sits where the Cowlitz and Columbia rivers meet and shares a border with Kelso, the county seat. Interstate 5 runs through the corridor, State Routes 4 and 432 connect to Kelso and Wahkiakum County, and the Lewis and Clark Bridge on State Route 433 crosses the Columbia to Rainier, Oregon. RiverCities Transit runs buses between Longview and Kelso.

How does Longview's weather affect a house you want to sell?

Longview's weather is wet, windy and often overcast, so buyers and inspectors look hard at roofs, gutters and drainage. The city sits in a small gorge, about 80 miles inland, and it tends to run several degrees cooler than Portland. Fall brings fog, rain starts in earnest by early to mid November, and winter can bring windstorms. The Columbia River gorge also channels summer evening winds, with gusts that can reach 30 to 40 miles per hour.

Before you list or accept an offer, walk the outside of the house with that climate in mind.

  • Check the roof surface and flashing for lifted or missing pieces after wind events.
  • Clear gutters and confirm downspouts carry water away from the foundation.
  • Look for damp spots in crawl spaces and along the lowest walls.
  • Trim tree limbs that overhang the roof or the power line.

Fixing these items first gives buyers fewer reasons to ask for credits.

Which schools serve Longview, and does it matter for a sale?

Longview Public Schools serves the city, and school assignment is one of the first things buyers with children ask about. The district runs eight elementary schools, three middle schools (Cascade, Monticello and Mount Solo) and two high schools, R. A. Long and Mark Morris. Lower Columbia College, founded in 1934, is based in Longview, and St. Rose Catholic School and Three Rivers Christian School operate in the city as private options.

What permits and records should a Longview seller check?

Start with the city's Community Development office, which issues building, electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits and handles zoning and code compliance. It is at 1525 Broadway Street in Longview City Hall, open Monday through Thursday from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. and closed on Fridays. The phone number is 360-442-5086 and the email is permits@ci.longview.wa.us. The city also keeps archived and recent property records online.

Use that office to answer three questions before you sell.

  • Did the owner before you, or you, pull permits for additions, a finished basement, a new deck or a re-roof?
  • Is there any open code compliance case on the property?
  • Does the lot's zoning allow what the current layout shows, such as an accessory dwelling or a second kitchen?

You can still sell a house with unpermitted work, though it often turns into a repair credit, a price cut or a lender question at closing. A cash buyer will usually take the house with the work as it stands and adjust the offer. Your seller disclosure should describe the work honestly either way.

What does Washington law require from a Longview seller?

Washington law makes most sellers of improved residential property deliver a completed disclosure statement, and it makes the seller pay the real estate excise tax in most sales. Under RCW 64.06.020, the statement is due within five business days after both sides accept a written contract, unless you agree otherwise in writing. After delivery, the buyer has three business days to rescind the agreement.

The real estate excise tax is a state tax with a local add-on. The Department of Revenue says the seller usually pays it and that it is due to the county treasurer in the county where the property sits, on the date of sale. For the state portion, RCW 82.45.060 sets a graduated schedule, and the Department lists new thresholds for sales beginning January 1, 2027.

  • 1.1 percent on the part of the price up to $551,000.
  • 1.28 percent on the part from $551,000 to $1,551,000.
  • 2.75 percent on the part from $1,551,000 to $3,051,000.
  • 3 percent on any part above $3,051,000.

Sales that close before 2027 use the Department's earlier breakpoints of $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. Ask the Cowlitz County Treasurer which local rate applies to your address and what the combined amount will be at your price. With a median home value near $361,600, most Longview sales fall in the lowest band.

How do Cowlitz County property taxes work when you sell?

Cowlitz County mails tax bills each February, and the two payments are due April 30 and October 31. A payment mailed to the Treasurer at 207 N 4th Ave in Kelso must be postmarked by the due date, and late payments carry interest and penalties. When you close in the middle of a tax period, the title or escrow company usually prorates the bill between you and the buyer, so ask for the proration line on your settlement statement.

If you think the assessed value is wrong, call the Assessor at 360-577-3010 and talk with an appraiser. To protect your appeal rights you must also file a petition with the Board of Equalization, at 207 4th Avenue N in Kelso. The county says the petition must be filed or postmarked by July 1 of the assessment year or 30 days after the value notice was mailed, whichever is later. A phone call does not reserve the right to appeal.

How should you compare a cash offer with a listing in Longview?

Compare the net amount you would receive after every cost, not the headline price. A listing price is reduced by agent commissions, the excise tax, repairs the buyer requests and the carrying cost of every month the house sits unsold. A cash offer is usually lower, but it can remove several of those costs and shorten the timeline.

Ask each buyer the same questions: what is the exact price, what closing date can you commit to, who pays the excise tax and title costs, and is the offer contingent on an inspection or on financing. Have a title company or attorney review the purchase agreement before you sign.

More questions about Longview, WA

Do I have to make repairs before selling my Longview house?

No, Washington does not require repairs before a sale. You do have to complete the seller disclosure statement honestly, and a buyer who sees defects may ask for a lower price or credits. Selling as-is to a cash buyer avoids the repair work but usually lowers the offer.

Who pays the real estate excise tax in a Longview sale?

The seller usually pays. The Department of Revenue says the tax falls on the seller in most sales, and if the seller does not pay it, the buyer becomes responsible. It is paid to the Cowlitz County Treasurer on the date of sale, so budget for it when you estimate your proceeds.

When are Cowlitz County property taxes due?

The two annual due dates are April 30 and October 31. The county mails bills each February, and a mailed payment counts as timely when it carries a postmark on or before the due date. Late payments add interest and penalties.

How long does the seller disclosure take in Washington?

Delivery is due within five business days after both sides accept a written contract, unless you agree to a different time in writing. The buyer then has three business days to rescind. RCW 64.06.020 contains the form and the timing.

Can I sell a Longview house with unpermitted work?

Yes, you can sell it, but you should disclose it. Contact the city's Community Development office at 360-442-5086 to see which permits are on file. Buyers who use a loan may ask for the work to be permitted or priced in, while a cash buyer may take the house as it stands and adjust the offer.

What drives demand for houses in Wenatchee?

Tree fruit built the local economy, and Wenatchee still calls itself the Apple Capital of the World. When the Great Northern Railway reached the valley in 1893, it carried wheat, apples and other products to outside markets, and by the early 20th century the local chamber of commerce was advertising the region as the home of the world's best apples. Stemilt Growers moved its headquarters to Olds Station in Wenatchee in 1975 and grew into the largest fresh market sweet cherry shipper in the world.

Industry has shifted too. The Alcoa smelter in Malaga announced in November 2015 that it would shut down, and tourism and information technology are described as growing areas of the regional economy. Forbes named the Wenatchee Valley one of the top 25 places to retire in 2019, and the Apple Capital Recreation Loop Trail, a 10-mile loop on both banks of the Columbia, is a draw for buyers who want to be outdoors. How does Wenatchee's climate affect a house?

Wenatchee has a semi-arid climate with cold winters and hot, dry summers. Annual precipitation averages only about 9 inches, the record high is 113 degrees and the record low is minus 19. Keep roof and plumbing records handy, since a buyer will ask about both.

The city's Building Division FAQ publishes the design numbers that local work must meet:

  • Roof snow load of 40 pounds per square foot
  • Climate zone 5B
  • Design wind speed of 85 mph
  • Footing and foundation freeze depth of 18 inches
  • Waterline depth of at least 3 feet, and 5 feet under a driveway

Houses on the hillsides ringing the city sit against ridges that form a wall around the west and south sides, so slope, drainage and retaining walls deserve attention. The FAQ exempts most retaining walls up to four feet high from a permit, though setbacks and shoreline rules still apply.

Which schools and roads matter to Wenatchee buyers?

The Wenatchee School District provides public K-12 education and serves Malaga, Olds Station, South Wenatchee, Sunnyslope and Wenatchee Heights. The city has seven elementary schools, three middle schools and one high school, Wenatchee High School. Check which attendance area your address falls in before you list.

U.S. Route 2 passes less than a mile north of city limits near Sunnyslope, and U.S. Route 97 also passes north of the city. State Route 28 runs through East Wenatchee across the river. The Columbia has three bridges: the Richard Odabashian Bridge and the Senator George Sellar Bridge for vehicles, and the Old Wenatchee Bridge for pedestrians. Link Transit provides bus service across Chelan County and into parts of Douglas County, and the airport at Pangborn has Alaska Air service.

Do I need a permit before selling a Wenatchee house?

Only if you do the work first. The city's Building Division says that if you have to ask, you probably need a permit, since permits are required for any building or structure that is erected, constructed, enlarged, altered, repaired, moved, improved, removed, converted or demolished. Painting, papering and similar finish work is exempt.

Other exemptions in the FAQ include one-story storage sheds up to 200 square feet with the required separation from structures and property lines, and decks no more than 30 inches above grade that do not serve a required exit door. Replacing a leaking sink trap needs no permit, but moving a fixture or installing new drain or supply lines generally does. If a furnace fails, emergency replacement can be done right away, though you should then get the permit and an inspection once the work is finished.

The Building Division is at City Hall, 301 Yakima, and can be reached at (509) 888-3244, Monday through Friday from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. For rules on short-term rentals or rentals in general, ask the city's Community Development staff or Chelan County before you promise a buyer that use.

How is the deed handled in Chelan County?

Any instrument that conveys property goes through the Chelan County Treasurer before the Auditor records it. The Auditor's recording instructions say the Treasurer processes the Real Estate Excise Affidavit and collects either the excise tax due or a $10 processing fee when the transaction is exempt. The documents are then forwarded to the Auditor for recording. Even an exempt transfer needs the affidavit.

State law says the same thing in RCW 82.45.090, which keeps a deed out of the auditor's hands until the tax is paid or marked not due. Ask the Chelan County Treasurer for the total owed on your price, since it has a state part and a local part.

The Auditor accepts only properly formatted documents with original, notarized signatures and the correct fee. The common reasons for refusal are:

  • A missing parcel number
  • A first-page top margin under 3 inches
  • Illegible text
  • A missing legal description
  • An inadequate fee

Sellers of improved residential property also complete the state condition form in RCW 64.06.020. The default deadline to deliver it is five business days after the buyer and seller sign a contract.

Yes. Cash buyers often purchase houses as they stand. The state disclosure form in RCW 64.06.020 still goes to the buyer, with any problems you know about listed.

What does the Chelan County Treasurer do in a sale?

The Treasurer processes the Real Estate Excise Affidavit and collects the excise tax due, or a $10 processing fee when the sale is exempt. Only after that does the Auditor record the deed.

Do small projects need a permit in Wenatchee?

Some do not. The city exempts painting, certain small sheds, retaining walls up to four feet and low decks. Moving a plumbing fixture or adding new supply or drain lines generally does require a permit, so call the Building Division at (509) 888-3244.

What snow load and freeze depth apply to Wenatchee homes?

The city lists a 40 pound per square foot roof snow load and an 18 inch freeze depth for footings and foundations. The climate zone is 5B, and design wind speed is 85 mph.

Which school district covers Wenatchee?

The Wenatchee School District serves the city along with Malaga, Olds Station, South Wenatchee, Sunnyslope and Wenatchee Heights. It runs seven elementary schools, three middle schools and Wenatchee High School.

Where is University Place, and how did the city take shape?

University Place is a mostly suburban city in Pierce County on the west side of Tacoma, with waterfront on Puget Sound. It covers 8.34 square miles of land, sits at about 417 feet of elevation, and is bordered by Puget Sound to the west, Lakewood to the south, and Tacoma to the north and east, with Fircrest along part of the eastern edge.

The name goes back to the 1800s, when the University of Puget Sound bought land along Grandview Drive for a campus. The school ended up selling the land back for about $11,000. The area stayed unincorporated until the City of University Place was formed on August 31, 1995.

Chambers Bay is the best-known landmark. The links-style golf course opened in 2007 and hosted the 2010 U.S. Amateur and the 2015 U.S. Open. The 28-acre University Place Town Center, built in the late 2000s and early 2010s, holds the city hall, a Pierce County Library branch, the police offices, a public plaza and a mix of homes and shops. The Village at Chambers Bay has metered parking on Market Place, and the city runs parking enforcement patrols there. Cirque Park hosts community events and youth sports programs run with the Pearl Street YMCA, and the city invited residents to a Veterans Day celebration at Veterans Plaza in the park. For property tax details, call the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer at (253) 798-6111 for assessed values, statements and senior or disability exemptions, or the treasury line at (253) 798-8678. Starting in January 2027, more Pierce County homeowners who are 61 or older, or who have a qualifying disability, will see their property taxes reduced under an expanded state program.

Washington's seller disclosure law, RCW 64.06.020, gives the buyer three business days after delivery of the form to rescind the agreement unless both sides agree otherwise. If the seller does not hand over a completed form, the buyer may waive that right before or after signing the contract.

Listing makes sense when the house is in good shape and you can wait for showings and a buyer's financing. A cash offer fits better when the house needs repairs, belongs to an estate, or has to close on a set date.

Many Mount Vernon properties are in the 100-year floodplain, and the city tells owners to check FEMA's Map Service Center or ask Development Services for the flood zone and what it means for a parcel. Know your zone before you list, because buyers and lenders will ask.

The river has flooded downtown since the city's early days. Residents once built a sandbag wall six blocks long to hold it back, and the city bought a mobile flood wall in 2007 and finished a permanent flood wall in 2019. Floods still reached the area around Thanksgiving 2017 and again on November 15, 2021. Rain is part of the picture too, with NOAA normals showing about 32.7 inches of precipitation a year, roughly two thirds of it from October through March.

  • Look up your parcel on the FEMA Map Service Center or ask the city for the flood zone.
  • Gather any elevation certificate, flood insurance policy, or past claim records you have.
  • Answer the seller disclosure questions on flooding, standing water, and floodplains from what you know.

What is Mount Vernon like for homeowners and commuters?

The city grew around logging, then the Great Northern Railway, which arrived in 1891 and brought hundreds of new businesses and residents. Mount Vernon became the county seat in 1884 when it was chosen over La Conner.

Interstate 5 was built through downtown in 1969, which separated downtown from most of the residential district and opened farmland to the north for development. Today the area is known for the Skagit Valley Tulip Festival, which brings a downtown street fair each year.

The city runs a mayor-council government with a directly elected mayor on a four-year term and a seven-member council, so code changes pass through a council you can attend.

  • Skagit Station, built in 2004, connects Amtrak Cascades, Skagit Transit, Greyhound, and local taxis.
  • Skagit Transit runs a commuter bus to Everett Station, which connects with the Sounder train to Seattle.
  • State Route 9 runs parallel to I-5, and State Routes 536 and 538 link downtown and the Baker Heights area.
  • Bellingham International Airport is 25 miles north.

Which Mount Vernon permits should you check before selling?

Start with Development Services at 910 Cleveland Avenue, phone 360-336-6214, email permittech@mountvernonwa.gov. The Building Division reviews permits, interprets codes, inspects work, and enforces the code, and the city has adopted the 2021 International Codes with Washington amendments.

The city lists what needs no building permit, and some items still need a planning permit:

  • One-story detached sheds and playhouses of 200 square feet or less (a planning permit is still required).
  • Retaining walls not over 4 feet high from the bottom of the footing, unless they hold a surcharge.
  • Decks not more than 30 inches above grade and not over a basement, when a location permit is obtained.
  • Fences under 7 feet, but only with a fence permit from Development Services.
  • Residential re-roofs with a single existing layer and no deck repair.

New fences and fence replacements always need a permit: a planning permit under 7 feet, a building permit at 7 feet or taller. The city's design criteria list Seismic Design Category D1. If a past remodel never had a permit, ask the permit technicians how to resolve it before a buyer's inspector raises it.

What are the excise tax and recording steps in Mount Vernon?

Skagit County collects the tax and records the deed. The seller signs a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit with the deed, the tax goes to the county treasurer, and Washington law requires that deeds be recorded with the county auditor.

The state portion is graduated. Under thresholds that run through December 31, 2026, it is 1.1 percent on the first $525,000, 1.28 percent up to $1,525,000, 2.75 percent up to $3,025,000, and 3 percent above that. Sales closing from January 1, 2027 use breakpoints of $551,000, $1,551,000, and $3,051,000. The Department of Revenue says the local REET is added, that the tax is due on the date of sale, and that the date of sale is when the deed is notarized.

The Skagit County Treasurer can confirm the local rate and what to bring. Ask the same office how the current half of property tax is handled at closing. Under RCW 64.06.020, deliver the seller disclosure statement within five business days of mutual acceptance unless it is waived or exempt.

When does a cash offer make sense in Mount Vernon?

It makes sense when the house is in a flood zone and you do not want a financing contingency, when repairs are overdue, or when you inherited a home and want to close on your own schedule.

Ask any Mount Vernon buyer for proof of funds, a closing date in writing, and who pays the excise tax and title fees. Then compare the number to a listing: subtract excise tax, agent fees, and repair credits, and count the weeks the house would sit. Request an offer on your Mount Vernon address to see where it lands.

More questions about Mount Vernon, WA

Do I have to disclose flood risk when I sell a Mount Vernon house?

The statutory seller disclosure form asks about flooding, standing water, drainage problems, and whether the property sits in a floodplain, and you answer from your own knowledge. The city says many properties are in the 100-year floodplain, so check your zone through FEMA's Map Service Center or Development Services first.

Who do I call about permits for a Mount Vernon home?

Call the Development Services Department permit technicians at 360-336-6214 or email permittech@mountvernonwa.gov. The office is at 910 Cleveland Avenue, and it can also tell you your zoning district and flood zone.

Does a fence need a permit in Mount Vernon?

Yes. The city requires a permit for all new fences and replacements: a planning permit for fences under 7 feet and a building permit for fences 7 feet or taller.

How much state excise tax would a $472,300 Mount Vernon sale owe?

The state portion is $5,195.30, which is 1.1 percent of $472,300, the Census median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024. The local excise tax is added, so ask the county treasurer or your title officer for the total.

Is the excise tax due when the deed is recorded or when the sale happens?

It is due on the date of sale, which the Department of Revenue treats as the date the deed is notarized, even if the deed is recorded later. Interest and penalties apply if it is not paid within one month of the sale date.

How can I sell a house fast in Walla Walla, WA?

The quickest routes are a sale to a cash buyer or an as-is sale to an investor, because neither waits on a mortgage approval. A standard listing can still make sense if the house is in good shape, but it comes with showings, an appraisal and the buyer's loan timeline.

Walla Walla is the county seat of Walla Walla County, set in a valley in southeastern Washington about 6 miles north of the Oregon line. The city is compact, covering roughly 13 square miles, and it sits near College Place, which adds a second small city to the same housing market.

What do the Census numbers show for Walla Walla homes?

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Walla Walla gives a picture of the local housing stock and household base.

The population is nearly flat, so a seller should expect buyers to compare your house closely with others on the market rather than assume rising demand will carry it. The short commute, under 13 minutes on average, is a real asset when you describe the location.

What drives the Walla Walla economy and housing demand?

Agriculture, wine, education and corrections anchor the local economy. Wheat remains a significant crop, and the wine boom of the past three decades produced more than 120 wineries in the greater Walla Walla area by summer 2020. The Walla Walla Sweet Onion is Washington's official state vegetable and has its own festival each July.

  • Whitman College, an independent liberal arts college in the city
  • Walla Walla Community College, which has a winemaking and grape growing program
  • Walla Walla University in nearby College Place
  • Washington State Penitentiary, opened in 1886, with about 2,000 inmates and about 1,000 staff

The city began as Steptoeville in 1856 around Fort Walla Walla and was incorporated on January 11, 1862, so older neighborhoods near downtown carry a long building history. The 13-story Marcus Whitman Hotel, which opened in 1928, is the tallest building in the city.

How does Walla Walla's climate affect a house?

Walla Walla lies in the rain shadow of the Cascades, so annual precipitation is fairly low. It has a hot-summer Mediterranean climate, yet winters can still turn cold. The valley's grape growers know the risk well: a killing freeze hits about once every six or seven years.

The city's building permitting page sets technical design numbers that any repair or addition must meet:

  • Ground and minimum roof snow load of 30 pounds per square foot
  • Design wind speed of 110 mph
  • Seismic design category D
  • Frost depth of 24 inches
  • Ice shield underlayment required

If you have replaced a roof or added a structure, keep the permit paperwork to hand over at closing.

Which schools and roads matter to Walla Walla buyers?

Most of the city belongs to Walla Walla Public Schools, which runs seven elementary schools, two middle schools, one traditional high school (Wa-Hi) and two alternative high schools, Lincoln and Opportunity. The far western edge of the city is in the College Place School District. Private options include the Walla Walla Catholic Schools, with Assumption K-8 and DeSales High School, and several Christian schools.

U.S. Route 12 is the main east-west highway, and since 2003 the Washington State Department of Transportation has expanded it to four lanes between Pasco and Walla Walla, with the eighth section finished in June 2023. State Route 125 runs through town and into Milton-Freewater, Oregon. Valley Transit serves Walla Walla and College Place and has been fare-free since 2022, and the Walla Walla Regional Airport has commercial flights to Seattle-Tacoma twice a day.

Do I need a permit to fix up a Walla Walla house before selling?

If the work is structural, mechanical or plumbing related, yes, the city handles it through Development Services. The department issues permits and inspections for new construction, remodels, mechanical and plumbing work, signs and other land use activity inside city limits, and it adopted the 2021 International Building Codes.

Applications, payments and inspection requests moved online for permits processed after August 19, 2025. Older permits may still involve contact with the permit technicians for payment and inspections. For a project that is not clearly listed, ask Development Services before you start.

What if my Walla Walla house is a short-term rental?

The rules depend on which type of short-term rental you have. According to the city's short-term rental FAQ, a Type 1 rental is the owner's principal residence, either with rooms rented while the owner is present or the entire dwelling rented no more than 90 days a year. A Type 2 rental is a dwelling that is not the owner's principal residence.

City Council adopted Ordinance 2017-33, which bans new Type 2 rentals. Those that were lawfully operating before November 9, 2017 may continue as non-conforming uses, and that status runs with the property if the use has not been abandoned. A buyer of such a property must obtain a Type 2 permit and license at closing, with proof of ownership. The permit can be lost in several ways:

  • Use is presumed abandoned if the location was not rented at least a total of 29 days in the preceding year
  • Use ends if the location sits unrented for 6 consecutive months or more
  • A fourth nuisance violation leads to revocation, after fines of $750 and then $1,000

If you own a Type 2 rental, ask Development Services for the current permit status before you advertise the sale, since a buyer's offer may depend on it.

How is a deed handled in Walla Walla County?

RCW 82.45.090 puts the real estate excise tax in the hands of the treasurer of the county where the property sits, who acts as the state's agent. The county auditor then has no authority to take the deed for recording until payment is verified or the treasurer notes that nothing is due. In Walla Walla County that means a visit or mailing to the Treasurer first, then recording through the Auditor.

Ask the Walla Walla County Treasurer for the total excise tax at your sale price, since the tax combines a state and a local portion. A title or escrow company normally carries the affidavit and deed through both offices for you.

The seller also owes a written condition disclosure. RCW 64.06.020 prescribes the form for improved residential property, and the delivery deadline is five business days after a signed purchase contract, absent a different agreement. Receiving it gives the buyer three business days to back out.

More questions about Walla Walla, WA

Can I sell a Walla Walla house that needs repairs?

Yes. Investors and cash buyers often take houses with deferred maintenance. The seller disclosure form under RCW 64.06.020 still has to go to the buyer, and known defects or unpermitted work belong on it.

Can a new owner keep running my Walla Walla house as a short-term rental?

Only in limited cases. New Type 2 rentals are banned, but a lawfully established one that has not been abandoned keeps its non-conforming status with the property. The new owner must obtain a Type 2 permit and license at closing with proof of ownership.

What building design numbers apply to Walla Walla houses?

The city lists a 30 pound per square foot roof snow load, a 110 mph wind speed, seismic design category D and a 24 inch frost depth. Ice shield underlayment is also required. These apply to new work under the 2021 International Building Codes.

Who collects the excise tax when a Walla Walla house sells?

The county treasurer, acting as the state's agent under RCW 82.45.090. Recording waits until the tax is paid or noted as not due, so ask the Walla Walla County Treasurer for the figure at your price.

Which school district serves my Walla Walla address?

Most of the city is in Walla Walla Public Schools. The extreme western edge is in the College Place School District. Verify the boundary with the district for your street.

What should a seller know about Pullman, Washington?

Pullman is a college town in the Palouse, in the eastern part of Whitman County about 65 miles south of Spokane and 32 miles north of Lewiston, Idaho. The Census Bureau estimates 33,756 residents as of July 1, 2025, which is 2.6% above the April 2020 estimates base. Washington State University, the state's land-grant college, is the reason most buyers and renters come.

Settlers staked claims on the site in the 1870s, and the town was incorporated on April 11, 1888. The legislature created the land-grant college in 1890, and Pullman leaders offered 160 acres to win it. The city covers about 11 square miles, all of it land.

Selling here usually means thinking about two kinds of buyer: families who want to stay and investors who want a student rental. The city's rental registration and short-term rental rules, covered below, apply to the second group.

What rental rules apply to a Pullman house?

Owners of residential rental property must register with the City of Pullman under Pullman City Code 6.98. The Police Department's permits and licenses page lists a one-time registration fee of $15 per address and names the Code Enforcement Supervisor, at 509-334-0802, for questions.

Short-term rentals are a separate process under Pullman City Code chapter 17.109. The city's application instructions list what an owner submits:

  • A business license using NAICS code 721199, applied for before final approval.
  • Insurance and liability coverage as required by RCW 64.37.050.
  • A floor plan showing beds, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, fire extinguishers and an emergency egress light.
  • An evacuation plan and a plot plan showing off-street parking.
  • A $200 short-term rental fee, paid before review starts.

Approval can carry an occupancy limit of the number of sleeping rooms plus two. If your house runs as a rental, tell a buyer which registrations are current and hand over the paperwork.

How do Pullman's hills and weather affect a house?

Pullman sits across four hills of windblown loess: Military Hill, Pioneer Hill, Sunnyside Hill and College Hill. Elevation runs from about 2,342 to 2,575 feet, and downtown lies in a valley where Missouri Flat Creek and Paradise Creek join the South Fork of the Palouse River. Steep lots and drainage are worth documenting if your house sits on a slope.

Winters are cold and wet and summers are hot and dry. The city's building division publishes design criteria that give a sense of what houses must handle: a ground snow load of 30 pounds per square foot, a frost depth of 30 inches, energy code climate zone 5B, and a required ice barrier underlayment on roofs.

Pullman adopted the 2021 International Building and Residential Codes, effective March 15, 2024. Reroofing, residing and replacement windows often need no plan review, and the city can issue those permits online, over the counter or next day. Projects that change the structure or footprint go through plan review that can take four to six weeks.

Applications can be emailed to pwcd-admin@pullman-wa.gov, and the office is at 190 SE Crestview Street, Building A. Finish any open permit before you list, because a buyer's lender or inspector may ask about it.

Which schools and roads serve Pullman buyers?

The Pullman School District covers Franklin, Jefferson, Sunnyside and Kamiak elementary schools, Lincoln Middle School and Pullman High School, the city's only public high school. Pullman High is on Military Hill, and students can take Running Start courses through WSU and Spokane Falls Community College.

U.S. Route 195 and State Route 27 run north toward Spokane and the Palouse towns, US 195 also runs south to Lewiston, and State Route 270 connects Pullman with Moscow, Idaho. Pullman Transit serves residents and WSU students. The Census puts mean travel time to work at 14.6 minutes.

If your house is close to campus or a bus line, say so in the listing, since a 14.6-minute average commute is part of what makes the location attractive.

How much real estate excise tax does a Pullman seller owe?

The seller owes it. RCW 82.45.080 puts the excise tax on the seller, and the state portion is graduated: 1.1% up to $525,000, 1.28% from there to $1,525,000, 2.75% to $3,025,000 and 3% above. A local portion is added, so ask the Whitman County Treasurer which rate applies in the city.

At the Census median of $424,800, the state portion would be about $4,673. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue raises the thresholds to $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. The date that counts is the date the deed is notarized, so a closing signed in late December uses the 2026 thresholds.

The Whitman County Treasurer lists real estate excise tax among its duties, so the affidavit, deed and payment go to its office at 400 N Main Street in Colfax. Unpaid tax can create a lien on the property, and the buyer can become responsible if the seller does not pay.

How do Whitman County property taxes work at closing?

State law, RCW 84.56.020, sets April 30 and October 31 as the two payment dates, and a bill of $50 or less is due in full by April 30. Whitman County's treasurer page carries a notice that property taxes are due by October 31. Ask the Treasurer which schedule your parcel follows.

  • Treasurer: 400 N Main Street, Colfax, mailing address P.O. Box 550, phone 509-397-6230.
  • Office hours listed on the county site: 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Ask your closing officer to prorate the year and clear any unpaid half from sale proceeds.

Ask the Whitman County Assessor whether a senior, disability or other reduction applies to your parcel. If you are behind on taxes, call the Treasurer before you list. The Treasurer's page announced a tax foreclosure sale for November 7 to 10, 2025.

What are the ways to sell a house in Pullman?

A Pullman owner can list the house, sell directly, or take an as-is offer from a cash buyer. The deed and excise tax steps are the same either way.

  • Listing works best when timing lines up with the academic calendar and the house shows well.
  • A direct sale to an investor can fit a rental with tenants, deferred repairs or a lease that ends mid-year.
  • Ask each buyer how they handle tenant notice, registration records and the closing date.

More questions about Pullman, WA

What is the owner-occupied rate in Pullman?

The Census reports 32.0% for 2020 to 2024, meaning roughly two of every three occupied homes are rented. Expect many buyers to be investors or to ask about rental history.

Do I have to register a rental house in Pullman?

Yes. Pullman City Code 6.98 requires owners of residential rental property to register with the city, with a one-time $15 fee per address, according to the Police Department's licensing page.

What does a short-term rental permit cost in Pullman?

The city's application instructions list a $200 short-term rental fee, paid before review begins. You also need a business license under NAICS code 721199 and the insurance that RCW 64.37.050 requires.

How long does a Pullman building permit take?

Reroofing, residing and window replacement may be issued online, over the counter or next day. More involved projects take four to six weeks for plan review.

Who collects the excise tax when a Pullman house sells?

The Whitman County Treasurer in Colfax, because the tax is paid to the county where the property sits. The seller owes it under RCW 82.45.080.

Maple Valley incorporated on August 31, 1997. Because of King County's urban growth boundary, the city is split into sectors along Maple Valley Black Diamond Road (State Route 169). The Four Corners district at State Route 169 and Kent Kangley Road (State Route 516) is the main commercial area, and central Maple Valley is mostly residential. The city covers about 6.2 square miles and borders Covington, Renton, Kent and Black Diamond.

The city's population grew nearly 63 percent from 2000 to 2010, and the 2020 Census counted 28,013 residents. The Green to Cedar River Trail runs through the city, and Lake Wilderness City Park hosts the annual Maple Valley Days Parade each June.

How do the lakes and weather affect a Maple Valley house?

The city has Lake Wilderness, Lake Lucerne, Rock Creek and part of Pipe Lake within its limits, and the Cedar River passes just outside the northeast border. Nights are cooler and rainfall is heavier than in Seattle, and winter days run slightly colder than closer to downtown Seattle. Check the roof, gutters, drainage and crawl space before a buyer's inspector does.

If your property is on or near water, the city asks owners to contact Economic and Community Development before they remove trees, especially on lakefront lots, modify environmentally sensitive areas such as wetlands, slopes and streams, or build or replace a dock. Maple Valley's planning covers duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes, townhouses, stacked flats, courtyard apartments and cottage housing, and a property with a single-family home may add two accessory dwelling units for three units total. The state deadline for compliance was June 2025.

Buyers who see development potential may pay attention to your lot size and zoning, so ask the department what your parcel allows before you describe it as a development site.

RCW 64.06.020 requires most sellers of improved residential real estate to deliver a disclosure statement within five business days after both parties accept a written contract, unless they agree otherwise. The buyer then has three business days to rescind.

The state rate is graduated, and a local rate is added on top. Earlier sales use $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. Since the Census median value in Maple Valley is $724,700, a typical sale is taxed partly at 1.1 percent and partly at 1.28 percent.

How do property tax dates and appeals work for a Maple Valley owner?

King County bills the property tax, and state law fixes the schedule. Under RCW 84.56.020, taxes are due on or before April 30, and if you pay half by that date the rest is due by October 31. Residential property with four or fewer units accrues interest at 9 percent a year when delinquent, with no penalties. The statute asks treasurers to send tax statements by March 15 when the budgets and rolls are ready on time.

To dispute an assessed value, RCW 84.40.038 lets you petition the county board of equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the notice, or a longer period up to 60 days if the county has adopted one, whichever is later. The board can waive a late filing for good cause, such as serious illness or a natural disaster. Check your notice for the exact deadline and ask the King County Assessor or Treasury Operations about your account. At closing, the title company usually prorates the current bill.

Ask any cash buyer for the closing date and the costs it expects you to pay in writing, and have a title company or attorney review the contract.

Yes. The city's permitting page lists installing new windows or replacing existing ones as work that needs a building permit. Siding replacement and painting do not need one. Call Economic and Community Development at (425) 413-8800 if you are unsure.

What happens if past work on my Maple Valley house had no permit?

It can complicate a sale. The city says unpermitted modifications may require tear-down, vacating or costly repairs, and many lenders want proof of a final inspection. Sellers also have to disclose improvements and whether permits were obtained, so ask the city what is on file.

Can I add accessory dwelling units on a Maple Valley lot?

Often, yes. The city's middle housing FAQ says a property with a single-family home may add two ADUs, for three units total, under the rules adopted to follow state law HB 1110. Zoning and lot details vary, so confirm with the city first.

When are Maple Valley property taxes due?

Taxes are due April 30. If you pay half by then, the second half is due October 31, as RCW 84.56.020 provides. King County sends the bill, and delinquent taxes on residential property with four or fewer units carry 9 percent annual interest.

How do I appeal my assessed value in Maple Valley?

File a petition with the county board of equalization by July 1 or within the number of days stated on your value notice, whichever is later. RCW 84.40.038 sets 30 days, or up to 60 if the county chose that. Include your evidence of value.
