  • Gateway: a residential area south of the Town Center, with a commercial center at the I-5 and State Route 104 interchange.
  • Lake Ballinger and Melody Hill: the remaining two planning neighborhoods. Lake Ballinger is a 100-acre lake in the southwest that drains toward Lake Washington.

Name the neighborhood in your listing or cash offer request. It tells buyers which schools, roads, and transit stops apply.

How do commuters and employers shape Mountlake Terrace?

Most residents work elsewhere. In 2018 figures, only 3.2 percent of employed residents worked inside city limits, and 37.0 percent commuted to Seattle. The largest employer is Premera Blue Cross, with 2,446 employees in 2022.

Interstate 5 has interchanges at State Route 104 (244th Street Southwest), 236th Street Southwest, and 220th Street Southwest, and State Route 99 touches the western edge. The Mountlake Terrace transit station, which opened in 2009, has 890 parking stalls and has been served by Link light rail since the line to Lynnwood opened in August 2024. Community Transit runs local routes to Edmonds, Lynnwood, and Brier, and King County Metro serves the station from Shoreline, Lake Forest Park, and Kenmore. The Census Bureau puts the mean commute for city residents at 27.9 minutes, a number worth quoting in your listing.

Who provides schools and utilities in Mountlake Terrace?

Public schools belong to the Edmonds School District, which has five schools inside the city: one high school, one middle school, and three elementary schools. Mountlake Terrace High School opened in 1960, was rebuilt in 1991 on the same campus, and sits in the northeast corner of the city.

  • Electricity: Snohomish County Public Utility District.
  • Natural gas: Puget Sound Energy.
  • Water and sewer: Alderwood Water and Wastewater District.
  • Garbage, recycling, and yard waste: collected under city contract with Waste Management.

Tell buyers which providers serve the house so they can price the monthly bills.

What permit rules matter when you sell a Mountlake Terrace house?

Work done without a permit is the main risk. The city's permit FAQ says failing to get one before construction is a code violation that can bring fines, that you may have to obtain permits and pass inspection or restore the site, and that permit fees may be doubled as a penalty.

  • Window and siding installation, roofing, plumbing, electrical, and structural changes always need a permit.
  • Sheds over 80 square feet or over 6 feet high need one, and a garage turned into living space is a change of use that needs one.
  • Removing drywall and exposing framing needs one, even for a wall removal or remodel.
  • Like-for-like cabinet replacement, painting, and carpet do not.
  • Permits expire if work does not start and pass an inspection within 180 days.

The FAQ adds that an owner doing the work must live in the home, and that a contractor is required if you plan to rent or sell. Email the permit specialists at permitspecialist@mltwa.gov for a specific project, and check the posted counter hours before you visit.

What are the excise tax and recording steps in Snohomish County?

The Snohomish County Treasurer reviews the deed first, and the Auditor's Recording Division records it second. If excise tax is owed, the deed cannot be recorded until it is paid in full at the Treasurer's excise tax counter.

The counter is open Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., phone 425-388-3366, at 3000 Rockefeller Avenue in Everett. Recording is in the same building, open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., phone 425-388-3483, and mail submissions need the exact recording fee. Recording fees depend on document type and page count.

The state tax is graduated at 1.1, 1.28, 2.75, and 3 percent by price slice, with the first breakpoint at $525,000 through December 31, 2026 and $551,000 from January 1, 2027. The local rate is added, and the tax is due on the date of sale, which the Department of Revenue treats as the notarization date. The seller disclosure statement in RCW 64.06.020 is due within five business days of mutual acceptance unless waived or exempt.

When does a cash offer make sense in Mountlake Terrace?

It makes sense when the house needs updating, when a probate or move is on a deadline, or when you want to avoid repairs a buyer's lender would require. Older houses with deferred updates are a typical fit.

Ask any buyer for proof of funds, a written closing date, and who pays the excise tax and title fees. Then compare the offer against a listing's net after excise tax, agent fees, repairs, and carrying costs. Request an offer on your Mountlake Terrace address to see the numbers side by side.

More questions about Mountlake Terrace, WA

Can I sell a Mountlake Terrace house that has unpermitted work?

Yes, but expect it to come up. The city says work without a permit is a code violation, and you may have to obtain permits and pass inspection or return the site to its original condition. Ask the permit specialists about your case before listing, or sell to a buyer who takes the house as it stands.

Who records the deed for a Mountlake Terrace sale?

Snohomish County does. The Treasurer's Office reviews conveyance documents such as deeds for excise tax, and the Auditor's Recording Division records them after any tax is paid. Recording is at 3000 Rockefeller Avenue in Everett, phone 425-388-3483.

How much state excise tax would a $667,300 Mountlake Terrace sale owe?

The state portion is $7,596.44: $5,775 on the first $525,000 at 1.1 percent and $1,821.44 on the remaining $142,300 at 1.28 percent. The local excise tax is added, and sales closing after January 1, 2027 use higher breakpoints.

Which school district serves Mountlake Terrace?

The Edmonds School District. Five of its schools are inside the city: Mountlake Terrace High School, one middle school, and three elementary schools. Confirm your attendance area with the district before you advertise a school assignment.

Does the light rail station affect selling a Mountlake Terrace house?

It gives you a transit selling point. The Mountlake Terrace station has 890 parking stalls and has been served by Link light rail since the extension to Lynnwood opened in August 2024. Mention the station and the commute time when you describe the house.

How does selling a house in Mercer Island work?

You can list the house with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes it as-is. Each route ends the same way: a deed, an excise tax affidavit, and a recording with King County.

Mercer Island sits in the southern half of Lake Washington, with Seattle to the west and Bellevue to the east. The city limits match the island, which is about six miles long and up to four miles wide. The Census Bureau counts 25,422 residents as of July 1, 2025, living on 6.38 square miles of land, and the island has its own hazard maps, permit rules, and school district, all covered below.

A cash sale suits owners who do not want to schedule showings, finish repairs, or wait for a buyer to line up financing. Listing can bring a higher price when the house is clean, permitted, and ready for photos. The rest of this page covers the numbers and city rules that decide which route fits.

What do Census figures say about Mercer Island homeowners?

Mercer Island is an owner-heavy, high-value city: 67.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the Census Bureau lists the median owner-occupied value at $2,000,000 or more. Median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $219,069, and median gross rent is $2,502.

  • Households: 10,068, averaging 2.50 people each.
  • Residents 65 and older: 22.2 percent, so inherited and downsizing sales are common.
  • Living in the same house one year earlier: 86.8 percent, which points to long ownership.
  • Mean commute: 23.6 minutes.

If you have owned the house for a long time, pull its permit history before you list. It shows which additions and remodels the city has on file.

How much state excise tax does a Mercer Island seller owe?

Washington charges a graduated real estate excise tax on the sale price, and the seller usually pays it. For a $2,000,000 sale under the thresholds that apply through December 31, 2026, the state portion comes to $31,637.50.

Source: RCW 82.45.060 and the Department of Revenue REET page. Sales that close on or after January 1, 2027 use higher breakpoints of $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000.

The Department of Revenue says the local REET is added on top of the state amount. Ask your title officer for the exact local rate on your closing date. The tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, which the department treats as the day the deed is notarized, and unpaid tax can become a lien on the property.

Do slope and seismic maps affect a Mercer Island sale?

They can. The city maps four hazard areas on its GIS portal: seismic, steep slope, erosion, and potential slide. If your lot is in one of them, work on the ground or vegetation usually needs a permit, and buyers will ask about it.

The island formed as a glacial plateau with ravines, and its elevation runs from about 18 feet at the lake shore to about 394 feet near Rotary Park. The Seattle Fault crosses the northern part of the island. On lots flagged as erosion, potential slide, or steep slope, the city does not allow clearing, grading, filling, or foundation work between October 1 and April 1 unless a waiver is granted with a geotechnical evaluation. A geotechnical report from a Washington licensed engineer is required when a structure goes into a critical area.

If you plan a repair before selling, check the map first. A retaining wall or deck fix that would be exempt on flat ground can need review on a slope.

Do unpermitted projects matter when you sell on Mercer Island?

Yes. The city's Code Compliance planner handles work done without required permits, and a buyer's lender or inspector can ask about past remodels. The city's own rule is that exemption from a building permit does not exempt a project from building or land use codes.

Under MICC 17.14.010, a permit covers work that builds, enlarges, alters, repairs, moves, demolishes, or changes the use of a structure, and it covers electrical, gas, mechanical, and plumbing systems. The city lists 22 exceptions. Examples include:

  • One-story detached sheds, playhouses, and similar structures up to 200 square feet.
  • Fences up to 6 feet high.
  • Retaining walls up to 4 feet, measured from the bottom of the footing, on flat ground with no surcharge.
  • Decks and driveways not more than 30 inches above grade and not over a basement.
  • In-kind re-roofing where the sheathing is not replaced.

Those exceptions do not apply in flood hazard areas or critical areas unless the work is entirely inside an existing legal building. The city also lists accessory dwelling units, tree cutting without a permit, and vacant unsecured structures among its code compliance topics. Construction hours are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Friday and 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Saturday, with no work on Sundays or holidays.

What paperwork does a Mercer Island seller handle?

You complete a seller disclosure statement, sign a deed, and file a real estate excise tax affidavit. The disclosure is due within five business days of mutual acceptance unless the buyer waives it or an exemption applies, and the buyer then has three business days after delivery to rescind.

The statutory form in RCW 64.06.020 asks about title, easements, boundary disputes, assessments, zoning violations, water, sewer, and structural problems. Answer from what you actually know and attach explanations for any yes answer.

  • King County Assessor: property report with lot size, present use, and year built.
  • King County Recorder's Office: recorded plats, surveys, and deeds.
  • MyBuildingPermit.com: status of building and land use permits.
  • City Online Map Portal: permit files, sewer as-builts, and geotechnical reports tied to your parcel.
  • Residential certificate of occupancy: for most island houses, the permit card with the signed final inspection serves as the certificate.

The City of Mercer Island permit center is at 9611 SE 36th Street, and land use staff take calls at 206-275-7605.

What do schools, bridges and transit look like on Mercer Island?

The Mercer Island School District runs seven schools on the island: Lakeridge, Island Park, West Mercer, and Northwood elementaries, Islander Middle School, Mercer Island High School, and the Crest Learning Center. Enrollment was 3,993 students in 2024 to 2025.

Interstate 90 crosses the island on the Lacey V. Murrow and Homer M. Hadley floating bridges toward Seattle and on the East Channel Bridge toward Bellevue. Much of the freeway is covered by the Mercer Island Lid, which holds parks and the Mountains to Sound Greenway trail. Sound Transit's 2 Line station in the I-90 median opened on March 28, 2026 and has a park-and-ride with 447 stalls. The city maintains 75 miles of streets, and Puget Sound Energy supplies electricity and natural gas.

These details help when you write a listing or explain the property to a cash buyer, since the island has one freeway corridor and a short list of schools.

When does a cash offer make sense for a Mercer Island house?

A cash offer makes sense when time, condition, or paperwork would slow a listing. Inherited houses, homes with deferred repairs, properties with old permit gaps, and sales with tenants in place are the usual cases.

Compare the net, not the headline price. On a listing, subtract the state and local excise tax, any agent fee you agree to, repair credits, and carrying costs such as utilities and insurance during the weeks the house sits. On a cash sale, ask the buyer for proof of funds, a written closing date, and who pays the excise tax and title costs. Then request an offer on your Mercer Island address and weigh it against the list-and-wait numbers.

More questions about Mercer Island, WA

Who pays the real estate excise tax when a Mercer Island house sells?

The seller usually pays it. The Department of Revenue says the buyer becomes responsible if the seller does not, and unpaid tax can create a lien. The tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, and the local rate is added to the graduated state rate.

Can I sell a Mercer Island house with work that was never permitted?

Yes, but expect questions. The city's Code Compliance planner handles work without required permits, and the usual fix is a courtesy letter or correction notice that asks you to resolve the issue. A cash buyer may take the house as it stands, while a listing buyer's inspector or lender may ask for the permit history.

Does the seller disclosure form apply to every Mercer Island sale?

It applies to improved residential property unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt under RCW 64.06.010. The seller delivers it within five business days of mutual acceptance unless the parties agree otherwise, and the buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind.

Does a steep or low-lying lot change how I sell on Mercer Island?

It can. The city maps seismic, steep slope, erosion, and potential slide hazards. Permit exemptions that apply on flat lots do not apply in critical areas, and ground work on erosion, slide, or steep slope lots is limited between October 1 and April 1 unless the city grants a waiver.

Where do I find recorded deeds and the sale history for my Mercer Island property?

Use the King County Recorder's Office for recorded plats, surveys, and deeds, and the King County Assessor for values and sales history. The city's Online Map Portal also shows permit files and geotechnical reports tied to your parcel.
